newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists mainly upbeat on AEX.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists mainly upbeat on AEX.

text.p: Dutch chartists were mainly positive on the short-term outlook for the AEX index, but ABN AMRO switched by forecasting a downtrend in the coming week.
"Due to the relative short term overbought situation, we expect the index to lose some ground over the coming week," ABN AMRO said, adding it remained bullish for the medium and longer term.

Most other chartists continued to be optimistic for the the index in the coming days. "The short term uptrend of the AEX is still intact, however a bit overbought," said ING Barings, while JAAD said that it saw a decrease in volatility.

The AEX share index closed at 752.62 points last Friday, 10.83 points up from the previous week's close. The index started this week somewhat lower with the AEX share index dropping 2.86 points to 749.76 yesterday. But it gained almost six points early on Tuesday. Contributor Trend Pvs view Support Resistance

ABN AMRO - Within the longer term uptrend, the AEX is facing lack of momentum. Prices can correct and this can easily result in renewed test of old support levels in the area 735-730. The level of 732.5 is the 50 percent retracement level of the move up from 698 (4/3/97) to 767 (4/24/97) and 733 is a perfect 61.8 percent retracement of the recent short term uptrend from 712 (4/14/97) to 767 (4/24/97). Due to the relative short term overbought situation, we expect the index to loose some ground over the coming week. However, this is only a short term correction and on the medium and longer term we remain bullish.

ING BARINGS - The short term uptrend of the AEX is still intact, however a bit overbought. Intermediate support should be found at the lower side of last week's gap area 751. If this latter area gives way, the charts indicate a correction towards strong support at MA9 around 740. Money flow indicators show a rising slope, suggesting that investors continue to buy any price dip. It also shows that there is still liquidity on the sidelines waiting to pour into the market. The A/D (advances/decline) ratio of the Amsterdam stock market, though slowly improving, is still not rising. The A/D line indicates that there is still no leadership in the market.

However, we still favour a mildly bullish scenario given the powerful underlying 4-week uptrend. We stick to our short term price target at the market's previous highs around 780. Only a solid close above 780 should be considered to have the durable uptrend resumed. As history shows that major bull runs do not start with lack of leadership, we expect big trouble at the AEX' March intraday highs of around 780. An unsuccesfull test of 780 should be followed by another sharp correction. First support should be found at the upper side of the previous trading range around 740. A fall below 730 is required to delay further positive scope.

JAAD - After record highs in the volatility, the situation seems to have stabilised a little bit. This decrease in volatility causes support and resistance to close in on current prices. Overall opinion: mostly sunny weather, with a small chance of sudden rainshowers.

RABO SECURITIES - Finally the barrier at 745 was broken, which paved the path for a further rise of the index. The next target can be found at 779, the old top formed in March of this year. Old resistance at 745 should now provide solid support underneath the market.

MEESPIERSON - The short term technical outlook for the AEX is rather bad, due to the worsening charts of the dollar and the bunds (they have reached their resistance levels). We expect the index will test its short term support at 742. Nevertheles we expect this support level will hold, as long as wall Street holds around current levels.
